bullets.title: Fed speakers hold hawkish-to-neutral line; inflation still top priority, rate path uncertain
bullets.body: Fed's Daly and Schmid both flagged inflation as the #1 concern, with Daly saying forward guidance is "not good at this juncture" and explicitly stating policy is "in a good place." Schmid asked how long the Fed should hold steady. Both cited energy/tariff prices as the primary inflation driver; Daly noted AI productivity gains are "not yet seen in data" and warned against 1990s analogies. IMF separately pushed its forecast for the Fed reaching 2% to end-2027 and urged caution.

bullets.title: Payrolls Friday setup: survey consensus at 110k, investors see strong print as risk-off
bullets.body: 22V survey found 47% expect mixed reaction to payrolls, 30% risk-off, 25% risk-on. The buyside consensus for payrolls is 110k vs sell-side 85k; 76% expect an above-consensus print. Critically, a strong print (>120k) is now viewed as risk-off, flipping the year-start framing. Weekly jobless claims already disappointed at 225k vs 215k estimate, highest since February; Q1 productivity came in at 0.3% annualized vs 0.8% estimate; unit labor costs +1.8% vs 2.5% est.

bullets.title: Tech/Nasdaq diverges sharply from Dow; AVGO -15% worst earnings reaction ever drives intraday rotation
bullets.body: NASDAQ 100 opened down ~1-1.2% while the Dow hit record highs (+1.6%, 790 pts). Broadcom's 3Q AI revenue guide of ~$16B missed consensus near $17.2B, triggering its worst-ever earnings reaction at -15%; the $350B market cap loss exceeded Netflix's entire market cap. S&P 500 IT Index -1.4% while Communications +2.1% (led by GOOGL). Tech sector P/E at 47x TTM, 100th percentile for the past decade per Bespoke.

bullets.title: Energy shock central: WTI near $93, oil inventories at 22-year lows, Iran war removes 14M bbl/day
bullets.body: JPMorgan global macro revised full-year 2026 GDP down 0.3pt to 2.3% with energy shock creating a 0.8% drag; global CPI revised up 100bp to 3.7%. IMF flagged global oil prices 3% above April baseline assumptions. Iranian crude exports hit multi-year lows below 300K bpd; fewer than 50 laden non-Iranian tankers transited Hormuz in May. US oil and petroleum inventories hit 22-year lows. Bessent said Russia oil waivers have helped keep prices down; future waivers will be country-by-country. Trump told aides he won't resume all-out Iran attacks unless US troops are killed.

bullets.title: ISM Services PMI 54.5, Prices Index at highest since August 2022 at 71.3
bullets.body: ISM Services PMI rose 0.9 points to 54.5 but inflation details were hawkish: the prices paid index reached 71.3, highest since August 2022 and above 60% for 18 consecutive months. Employment sub-index remained subdued. Separately, Challenger layoffs rose 16% MoM and 3% YoY in May with AI cited as the biggest driver; 88k AI-attributed job cuts YTD is 60% above all of 2025.

bullets.title: Blackstone private credit fund gates redemptions at 5% amid 10% investor requests
bullets.body: Blackstone's $79B BCRED received redemption requests for ~10% of shares outstanding in Q2 but will only honor 5%, matching peers imposing similar gates. Signals liquidity stress building in private credit markets; broader alternatives complex under pressure.

bullets.title: Goldman maintains equity overweight; buy dips as returns moderate after record Dow
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs expects equity returns to moderate after the strong rally to near-record highs but maintains a 12-month overweight stance. Dow hit an all-time high intraday (+1.6%). S&P 500 advance/decline line was tracking its best reading in nearly 2 months despite index-level flatness. Barclays separately recommended buying stock protection.

bullets.title: AI productivity gap widening: capex surges but no macro productivity signal yet
bullets.body: Q1 productivity growth of 0.3% annualized (vs 0.8% est) provides no evidence of AI-driven gains; JPMorgan note flags productivity trend stable at ~2.1%. 22V survey showed growing investor concern about rising AI costs and whether productivity/margin gains are actually being realized. Bank of England's Bailey warned markets may be "exaggerating the speed of AI pass-through." Separately, agentic traffic reportedly surpassed human traffic on HTML webpages globally per Cloudflare Radar data.

bullets.title: Tech sector at record 39.7% of S&P 500; Tech+Comms now ~50% of index
bullets.body: Tech sector weighting hit 39.7% of S&P 500 on Tuesday, nearly 5 percentage points above the March 2000 dot-com peak. Tech and Communications combined represent approximately half of index market cap. Retail bullish options activity in mega-cap tech is approaching near-record levels, with bullish trades comprising nearly two-thirds of retail opening options flow.

bullets.title: Prediction markets: Fed holds at 98% in June, 70% chance of zero cuts all year; Hormuz reopening only 17%
bullets.body: Kalshi/prediction market data shows Fed hold in June at 98%, July at 93%. 70% odds of zero Fed cuts in 2026; 40% odds of at least one hike. Hormuz normalization by end of June at only 17% (-18% WoW). US recession probability by end-2026 at 18%. WTI above $120 only 10% likely.

bullets.title: Coatue's Laffont: AI ecosystem ~$140B now, $300B by year-end; hyperscalers remain primary beneficiaries
bullets.body: Thomas Laffont at All-In estimates AI revenue at ~$140B currently, potentially $300B this year and doubling by 2027. Hyperscalers (MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL) fund and enable the buildout; META and GOOGL already monetizing with ~25% of ads incorporating AI. Private AI companies scaling faster than prior software precedent. Venture concentration intensifying: funding per unicorn up ~5x since 2021.

bullets.title: NVDA launches Vera Rubin (Q3 2026), Nemotron 3 Ultra (5x faster inference, 30% lower cost), secures $124B supply commitments
bullets.body: At BofA Tech Conference, NVIDIA guided Vera Rubin platform for Q3 2026 with $124B in supply purchase commitments; hyperscaler and AI cloud each ~50% of revenue with hyperscaler growing faster. Separately, Nemotron 3 Ultra targets agentic workloads with 5x faster inference and 30% lower cost. NVDA also invested $2B each into Coherent and Lumentum for Spectrum-X Ethernet Photonics (entered production May 31), countering CPO cannibalization fears.

bullets.title: T and VZ each drop 3%+ after Supreme Court upholds FCC enforcement authority in wireless fine case
bullets.body: Supreme Court ruled against T and VZ, affirming FCC's authority in wireless enforcement fine cases. T fell 3.3% and VZ fell 3.8% on the ruling. The S&P 1500 Communications Index still gained 2.1% on the day, driven by GOOGL.

bullets.title: Databricks delays IPO beyond 2026 citing AI-IPO glut; Quantinuum debuted at $68-75, 20x oversubscribed
bullets.body: Databricks CEO explicitly said current year conditions are unfavorable for IPO amid the flurry of AI offerings. Meanwhile, Quantinuum priced at $60 and opened at $68-75 (18-25% pop), was 20x oversubscribed, and is being called the largest quantum IPO ever at ~$18.4B valuation — cited as a validation moment for the quantum sector.

bullets.title: AVGO earnings: 6th consecutive triple play but AI revenue guide disappointment was historic
bullets.body: Broadcom beat Q2 estimates but the 3Q AI revenue guide of ~$16B missed consensus of ~$17.2B and provided no FY27 upside; Macquarie downgraded to Neutral. The stock's ~15% decline was its worst-ever earnings reaction, with two of its biggest-ever post-earnings drops occurring in the last three quarters. Analyst Harlan Sur (JPM) is projecting $300B in AVGO AI revenue by 2028, implying the long-term thesis remains intact but near-term bar was set too high.

bullets.title: AAPL: WWDC focus on Siri/AI catch-up; near-term demand driven by hardware, not AI; services monetization years away
bullets.body: Citi (Buy, $315 PT) views WWDC as an AI catch-up phase — Apple is closing competitive gaps, not breaking new ground. Near-term iPhone demand is hardware/share-gain driven; IDC revised global iPhone demand to -5% (from -8%) and China to -3% (from -9%). iPhone 16 already supports most Apple Intelligence features, limiting upgrade pull-forward. Separately, Apple said its App Store ecosystem hit $1.4T. Apple's revamped Siri will rely on Google's NVIDIA chip infrastructure at September launch.

bullets.title: Oil market cross-currents: WTI at ~$93 after 3-day rally, crude inventories at multi-decade lows
bullets.body: WTI crude pulled back 3.1% to ~$93 after a 3-day gain of >9%; Brent fell 3.5% to $94.37. US oil+SPR inventories at 22-year lows. Natural gas +3.8% to $3.34, best in 4 months, on below-consensus storage build (+95 Bcf vs +99 Bcf est). Trump said oil prices will "fall like a rock" and Bessent confirmed Iran conflict "has been halted." 10-yr yield above 4.5% represents a historical threshold where valuation headwinds for equities intensify.

bullets.title: Credit vol setup: IG screening cheap vs HY; front-end implieds at <1 bp/day breakeven, midterms driving Oct/Nov payer interest
bullets.body: MS credit derivatives desk reports realized vol grinding at ~0.6 bps with IG front-month 50-delta calendar steep at ~93rd percentile. Fast money rolling vol shorts and buying payer ratios; real money rolling outright 25-delta payers to September. IG screening cheap versus HY; fast money selling further-dated HY payers. Midterm elections beginning to drive interest in October-November downside vols as a potential catalyst.

bullets.title: Semiconductor ex-memory revenues forecast to exceed $1T by 2029; AI infrastructure bottlenecks shifting to MicroLED optical interconnects
bullets.body: One analyst projects ex-memory semiconductor revenues will exceed $1T in 2029, a historically high threshold. AI infrastructure bottleneck analysis suggests the next constraint after GPUs, HBM, and optics will be MicroLED optical interconnects, where Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron are all active. TSMC acknowledged capacity constraints: "We can only support so much."

bullets.title: Payrolls preview: labor market signals mixed ahead of Friday; 1-in-3 working-age men exiting workforce
bullets.body: Initial claims rose to 225k (highest since February) vs 215k estimate. Challenger layoffs hit highest May level since 2020, with ~1.7M total layoffs in May per Revelio Labs; AI cited as top reason for 3rd consecutive month. Separately, 1 in 3 working-age men now exiting the workforce (WSJ), and most common jobs pay below the $69,770 national average, flagging structural labor market pressure on consumers.
